summary.intent: Add --kind flag to memory-loop refresh to focus generation on a specific memory kind (repo_rule, skill_patch, etc.), and print the generation threshold right after the scope line during refresh output.
summary.outcome: Implemented --kind flag with prompt narrowing (kind enum + directive), post-generation filtering, history tracking, and threshold/kind printing after the scope line. All tests pass with no new lint issues.

repo: TUI settings tab saves to memory-loop.json, but refresh reads from settings.json — state loading must happen before threshold resolution for TUI overrides to take effect.
Store rebuild in runMemoryLoopRefresh was missing InjectionScopes, GenerationThreshold, and GenerationOverrides fields, causing them to be lost on each refresh.
GenerateInput struct in memoryloop/generator.go is the central place to pass generation configuration; KindFocus was added there alongside threshold/scope fields.
BuildPrompt already constructed the kind enum as a JSON schema constraint; narrowing it to a single value is the correct mechanism to focus LLM output.
RefreshHistory in memoryloop.go is the right place to track what kind was targeted, for auditability.

code.finding: The LLM prompt encodes kind as a JSON schema enum listing all five kinds; narrowing this to the requested kind is how kind-focused generation is implemented.
State loading (loadMemoryLoopState) must precede threshold resolution so TUI-saved settings override settings.json values, matching how Mode/MaxInjected/ActivationPolicy are handled.

workflow: Pre-existing lint issues (goconst 'balanced', maintidx) should be verified by stashing changes and running lint on the base before attributing issues to new code.
All runMemoryLoopRefresh call sites in tests must be updated when the function signature changes — grep for the function name before finalizing signature changes.

friction: A git checkout during lint verification accidentally reverted in-progress changes, requiring both edits to be re-applied from scratch.
The stash/restore workflow for verifying pre-existing lint issues caused temporary loss of work due to checkout side effects.
open_items: The --kind flag filters post-generation as a safety net, but the LLM may still generate off-kind results at low rates; no metric currently tracks LLM compliance vs. filter drop rate.
Kind-specific prompt directives are hardcoded strings; no mechanism exists to tune them per-project or per-user.
